raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret this as one acquisition-email brief—not finished copy—for the selected product-aware audience, narrowed per the current dossier to freelancers delivering a client project. The email will invite them to inspect the planner’s documented 16-week, goal-breakdown and monthly/weekly/daily structure without assuming their tools, pains or past failures.

intent.reason_now: A freelancer may be starting a focused client-project push that can be planned across the product’s documented 16-week format.
intent.desired_action: Look inside the Your Plans on Paper productivity planner.

raw_plan.reader: A goal-driven freelance professional considering a paper planning structure for a focused 16-week client project.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
raw_plan.reader_scope: Only freelancers delivering a client project within the selected broader audience; do not generalise the fit to every goal-driven professional.
raw_plan.promise: A freelancer can give a substantial client project a bounded paper structure across 16 undated weeks, with goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
raw_plan.orientation: A paper productivity planner for an individual professional organising daily work toward a substantial goal over a focused 16-week period.
raw_plan.arc: In one step, move the reader from recognising another paper planner to seeing a specific 16-week planning mechanism they can inspect for their next client project.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: Because this is one acquisition email to a product-aware reader, it should lead immediately with the checkable mechanism and a low-friction product-page action. It deliberately avoids the researched continuous-calendar problem because the dossier marks that fit as only partial and does not establish a rolling view or links between notes and dates.

emails.selection_reason: The bounded 16-week format directly matches the selected audience’s focused-push constraint, while goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily pages give a concrete planning mechanism a freelancer can judge for a client project.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a suitable client project, the reader can organise one substantial goal across a bounded paper cycle and connect the larger plan with monthly, weekly and daily planning.
value_case.mechanism: The planner provides 16 weeks of undated pages, supported by goal breakdowns, plus pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning.
decision_conditions: The useful fit is a project that can be organised within a 16-week planning cycle.
The evidence does not establish a rolling current-day calendar or links between notes and dates.

emails.target_audience: Freelancers delivering a client project who are starting a focused 16-week push and want to plan away from screens.
emails.job: Earn a product-page visit from a qualified freelancer who wants to decide whether this planner’s structure suits an upcoming client project.
emails.single_idea: Give one client project a defined paper planning cycle: 16 undated weeks, goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily pages in one productivity planner.
emails.mechanism: Start with the project goal, break it down within 16 undated weeks, and use the planner’s monthly, weekly and daily pages to organise the work at different time horizons.
emails.belief_shift: Before: this may be another attractive paper planner. After: its specific 16-week, goal-breakdown and monthly/weekly/daily structure may be relevant to a bounded client project and is worth looking inside.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner provides a continuous current-day-centred view or exposes links between notes and dates.
Do not imply integration with Obsidian, calendars, MS 365 or any other installed tool.
Do not claim guaranteed project completion, improved productivity, time savings or better client outcomes.
Do not state or imply that the recipient has struggled with apps, missed deadlines or failed with another planning system.
Do not generalise this fit beyond freelancers delivering a client project.
Do not turn planning away from screens into a claim that screens or digital tools are inherently ineffective.
Do not add unsupported pricing, testimonials, delivery promises or competitive-superiority claims.
Do not dilute the email with wedding, photo-book, journal, sustainability or packaging propositions.
emails.objection: Will the planner show enough structure to connect a substantial project goal with planning at monthly, weekly and daily levels?
emails.tone: Artful, optimistic and concise, with calm practical specificity rather than productivity hype.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether this planner’s 16-week and monthly/weekly/daily structure suits the shape of a forthcoming client project.
emails.next_step_value: The product page offers a look inside the Your Plans on Paper planner, whose documented contents include monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
emails.next_step_limit: Looking inside does not establish a rolling current-day-centred view, links between notes and dates, or results for the reader’s project.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open with the concrete 16-week client-project planning use case; avoid a generic productivity promise, an invented pain or an unsupported outcome.

events.body:
Give one client project a clear paper plan with Papier’s Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner. If the work can be organised within a 16-week cycle, this planner gives it a defined place to unfold.

Begin with the substantial goal, use the goal breakdowns, then organise the work across monthly, weekly and daily planning pages. The pages are undated, so the cycle can begin when the project does.

> **£25.00** — for the Your Plans on Paper planner.

On the product page, you can flick through the planner and see how its 16-week structure could suit the shape of a forthcoming client project.

events.body:
Start with one substantial client-project goal. If the work fits a 16-week cycle, break it down across undated pages and plan it at monthly, weekly and daily horizons.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is a softback spiral productivity planner designed for that focused paper cycle. Clear goal breakdowns connect the larger plan with the work you want to organise at each level.

The monthly pages hold the wider view. Weekly and daily pages bring the plan closer, giving the project a practical shape away from screens.

Flick through the planner on the product page to see its 16-week structure and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.

events.body:
When a client project fits a 16-week window, give its goal a paper home—and each planning horizon its own page. The undated format lets the cycle begin with the project, rather than a calendar date.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is a softback spiral productivity planner with **16 undated weeks**, clear goal breakdowns, and pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning. Use those page types to organise the project at different time horizons.

On the product page, you can flick through the planner and inspect the monthly, weekly and daily layouts before deciding whether their structure suits your client project. See the pages for yourself, then choose whether this is where your next 16 weeks take shape.
